approved: The Migration (Validation of Port Appointment) Bill 2018 confirms the validity of a 2002 port appointment at Ashmore and Cartier Islands, ensuring that illegal maritime arrivals who entered via that port between 23 January 2002 and 1 June 2013 remain classified as unauthorised maritime arrivals and, where applicable, fast-track applicants under the Migration Act 1958. The bill maintains the status quo and does not apply to cases where a court has already set aside or declared the appointment invalid.

The motion substituted words to note poor drafting of immigration legislation by successive Coalition governments, citing a 2002 gazette error by minister Ruddock that omitted coordinates for a port. Labor supported the bill while reiterating its asylum seeker policy of strong borders and regional resettlement, including accepting New Zealand's offer.

The Migration (Validation of Port Appointment) Bill 2018 confirms the validity of a 2002 port appointment at Ashmore and Cartier Islands, ensuring that unauthorised boat arrivals entering through that port between 23 January 2002 and 1 June 2013 remain classified as unauthorised maritime arrivals and, where applicable, fast-track applicants. The bill prevents legal challenges to the appointment that could undermine border protection policies.
